title: How did Rio become the capital of a European empire?
hook: Fleeing Napoleon, a European ruler went to govern from his colony.
summary: In 1808 the Portuguese court fled Napoleon to Rio; in 1815 Brazil became a kingdom united with Portugal, with Rio as its capital.

cardBlocks.text: In 1808, the seat of a European empire crossed the Atlantic. Threatened by Napoleon Bonaparte’s troops invading Portugal, the Portuguese royal family reached Salvador in January and Rio de Janeiro on 7 March, together with the court elite and the kingdom’s administration. Although still a colony, Brazil became, in practice, the seat of the Portuguese empire.

The plan was a short stay, but the court remained until 1821. On 16 December 1815, a law signed by Prince John raised Brazil to a kingdom and joined Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves in a single United Kingdom. Brazil was no longer a colony, and the new kingdom had Rio as its capital.
Fleeing Napoleon, the Portuguese court settled in Rio in 1808; in 1815 Brazil became a kingdom.

deepDiveBlocks.text: While still in Salvador, on 28 January 1808, the Prince Regent John opened Brazil’s ports to direct trade with other countries. Until then, the colony could trade with the world only through Portugal.

The United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves had its capital in Rio de Janeiro and lands in Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia. In historian Lilia Schwarcz’s words, from 1815 the whole empire was run by the United Kingdom, no longer by the old mother country.
